name: Security
blurb: Defensive security for your own code: secure coding, threat models, Semgrep/CodeQL triage, dependencies, secrets and CI hardening.
searches: Semgrep new rules or release this month
GitHub Actions supply chain attack security advisory new
secret scanning leaked keys new tool or technique
threat modeling LLM agent security new guidance OWASP
agent skill security review Claude Code new release

tests.prompt: Add an endpoint that fetches a user-supplied image URL and stores a thumbnail.
tests.good: Allowlists scheme and host, resolves all DNS records and rejects private/link-local addresses, disables redirects, caps size and type, and adds an abuse-case test.

tests.prompt: Scan this repo with Semgrep and tell me what matters.
tests.good: Confirms the repo is the user's, agrees rulesets first, runs with metrics off via run-scans.sh, merges SARIF, confirms each finding in code and separates needs-verification items.

tests.prompt: Review our GitHub workflow that runs on pull_request_target and comments with an AI summary.
tests.good: Flags checkout of PR head with secrets, expressions in run blocks, unpinned actions and broad permissions; proposes split jobs, env indirection, SHA pins and a tool allowlist.

tests.prompt: Our Next.js + Supabase app lets members upload receipts (images and PDFs) that only their own team should see. Before launch, harden the upload and download path and add tests proving one team can't open another team's files.
tests.good: States a short plan first: threat-modeling.md (scope section) and secure-coding.md here; storage through backend-databases (supabase.md: private bucket, RLS policies on storage.objects, short-expiry signed URLs, service_role key never in client code); tests through testing-qa (playwright-e2e.md or tdd-and-unit-tests.md). Confirms the app is the user's; allowlists types, caps size and checks magic bytes; stores under generated names; scopes every read to the caller's team; writes a cross-team abuse test that fails first; separates findings from hardening suggestions; proposes fixes as diffs; checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: Our Node API ships as a Docker image and the security reviewer keeps sending it back with a screenshot of hundreds of CVEs. Scan the image with Trivy, tell me which ones actually matter, and add a check to our GitHub Actions pipeline that fails the build on real problems but doesn't block us on things nobody can fix yet.
tests.good: Confirms the image and repo are the user's and builds or pulls exactly the image that ships; runs Trivy for vulnerabilities, secrets and misconfig, sorts results by severity and fixability, and checks reachability and base image before ranking, instead of pasting the raw count. The CI step uses --severity HIGH,CRITICAL with --ignore-unfixed and --exit-code 1, so unfixed CVEs do not block; Expiry and reason live in .trivyignore (exp:YYYY-MM-DD after the ID, reason as a # comment line) or .trivyignore.yaml (statement and expired_at, passed with --ignorefile); a VEX document marks a finding not_affected with a justification but Trivy documents no expiry for it, never a blanket ignore. The action or install is pinned to a commit SHA with minimal permissions: contents read, security-events write only if SARIF is uploaded. Handles the vulnerability database download limits or caching and keeps registry credentials in secrets. Recommends the actual fixes (slimmer or updated base image, rebuild, bump packages) as a diff for approval, and reruns the scan to show the count dropped.

tools.name: Semgrep
tools.why: Named the best free SAST scanner (30+ languages, custom YAML rules) and a top-5 SAST tool in 2026 round-ups (appsecsanta, Orca, expertinsights).

tools.name: CodeQL
tools.why: The SAST engine inside GitHub Advanced Security, a top-5 SAST tool in 2026 round-ups and the default scanner for any GitHub-hosted repo (appsecsanta, Corgea).

tools.name: Snyk
tools.why: Developer-first SAST/SCA/container/IaC platform repeatedly ranked top-3 for developer experience, and a vetted Claude connector added July 2026 (appsecsanta, claude.com connector page).

tools.name: Dependabot
tools.why: Built into every GitHub repo and the default SCA and update bot; named as the SCA piece of GitHub Advanced Security in 2026 round-ups (appsecsanta, getastra).

tools.name: GitHub secret scanning and push protection
tools.why: The default leak detector for GitHub repos (partner-pattern alerts plus push protection), listed beside Gitleaks and TruffleHog as the standard secrets layer in 2026 round-ups (getastra, appsecsanta).

tools.name: Gitleaks
tools.why: About 29.7k GitHub stars (MIT) and named with TruffleHog as the free secrets scanners to use in 2026 open-source AppSec stacks (Orca, appsecsanta).

tools.name: TruffleHog
tools.why: About 28.3k GitHub stars; the secrets scanner that verifies whether a found credential is live, named in every 2026 free-stack round-up (Orca, getastra).

tools.name: Trivy
tools.why: About 38.2k GitHub stars (Apache-2.0); the standard open-source scanner for container images, dependencies, IaC and secrets in 2026 stacks (Orca, appsecsanta).

tools.name: OWASP ZAP
tools.why: About 15.9k GitHub stars (Apache-2.0); the default free DAST scanner named in 2026 open-source AppSec stacks (Orca, getastra).

tools.name: Burp Suite
tools.why: The standard commercial web pentest proxy, with an official PortSwigger MCP server (about 1.2k stars) that connects Burp to Claude Desktop; no public scanning API on the free edition.

tools.name: SonarQube
tools.why: One of the most widely deployed code quality and security gates (7,500+ rules, 40+ languages) and ships an official MCP server and Claude Code plugin with secret-scanning hooks (SonarSource repos).

tools.name: Socket
tools.why: The leading behaviour-based package scanner for npm, PyPI and others, with an official MCP server (hosted at mcp.socket.dev) and a Claude Code hook that blocks risky installs; narrower than SCA suites.

tools.name: OSV-Scanner
tools.why: About 11.1k GitHub stars (Apache-2.0); Google's lockfile and SBOM scanner on the OSV database, the common ecosystem-neutral alternative to per-language audit commands.

tools.name: Checkov
tools.why: About 9k GitHub stars (Apache-2.0); the IaC scanner (Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes, Dockerfile) in 2026 open-source AppSec stacks (Orca, getastra).

tools.name: Strix
tools.why: AI-native open-source pentest agent with about 66.6k GitHub stars (Apache-2.0) that validates findings with real exploits and outputs SARIF; only linked from the router, no how-to.

tools.name: GitGuardian
tools.why: The commercial leader in secrets detection and the #1 security app on the GitHub Marketplace (500-600+ secret types); ggshield (MIT, about 2k stars) is a common pre-commit and CI gate, and an official MCP server lets Claude scan for leaks and handle incidents (appsecsanta, GitGuardian docs).

tools.name: npm audit / pip-audit
tools.why: The package managers' own vulnerability audits are the first SCA check almost every JavaScript and Python developer runs (built into npm/pnpm/yarn; pip-audit is the PyPA tool, about 1.4k stars, Apache-2.0); the guide already gives the commands, but the list had no entry for them.

tools.name: Checkmarx One
tools.why: Named a Leader in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Application Security Testing for the seventh time (2025) and the usual enterprise SAST/SCA platform; ships an official Checkmarx MCP server that supports Claude Code, so it is no longer only a SARIF hand-off.

tools.name: Veracode
tools.why: Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader for Application Security Testing (2025) covering SAST, SCA and DAST, widely mandated in enterprise and regulated teams; has a CLI and a community MCP server for Claude Code.

tools.name: Black Duck
tools.why: Gartner AST Magic Quadrant Leader for the eighth time (2025), highest in Ability to Execute six years running; the enterprise SCA standard (with Coverity SAST), and Black Duck SCA 2026.7 ships an official MCP server for Claude and other assistants.

tools.name: OpenText Fortify
tools.why: Gartner AST Magic Quadrant Leader 11 years running (2025); 44+ languages, the long-standing SAST in government and large enterprise, with IDE, Jenkins and GitHub Actions integrations; no agent skills or MCP found, so results come in as SARIF/FPR.

tools.name: Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool
tools.why: The free SDL tool for STRIDE-per-element data-flow-diagram threat models and the most cited free threat modeling tool in 2026 round-ups; threat modeling is a core job of this craft and the list had no tool for it. Windows-only, no API.

tools.name: OWASP Threat Dragon
tools.why: OWASP's open-source threat modeling tool (about 1.6k stars, Apache-2.0): data-flow diagrams with STRIDE, LINDDUN, CIA and PLOT4ai, web or desktop, models stored as JSON in GitHub/GitLab; the cross-platform free pick in 2026 round-ups.

tools.name: OWASP Dependency-Check
tools.why: About 7.7k stars (Apache-2.0); one of the most widely used open-source SCA tools, especially for Java/.NET via Maven, Gradle and Jenkins plugins (Orca, jit.io round-ups).

tools.name: GitLab application security
tools.why: GitLab's built-in SAST, secret detection, dependency, container and DAST scanners are the default for GitLab-hosted repos, the counterpart of CodeQL plus Dependabot (full set on Ultimate; agentic SAST fixes GA in 18.11, April 2026).
